0b5db31c-78f7-4194-814c-824348b60836.headline: Three Fangtooths, more kills, a structure lead, and Serath never died. One 0-5 fight later, the whole fucking base was gone.
0b5db31c-78f7-4194-814c-824348b60836.team: For most of this game we were the team taking the map. All three Fangtooths and the first Genesis Core went our way, we outkilled them 27 to 23, and we led four structures to three going into the last fight. Nobody solved Serath: no deaths all game, and four of our five deaths in the late fight we lost 1-5. Then we lost a fight 0-5, and both inner towers, an inhibitor and our Core fell during and right after it, with the Genesis Core going to them.
0b5db31c-78f7-4194-814c-824348b60836.lossReflection: The better plan for the last stretch was to stop gambling the lead on even fights. With every Fangtooth and a structure lead already in hand, one inner tower was cheap and the base was not. The alternative was to concede that tower and fight under the next one with all five together, Aurora and Kwang holding their crowd control for Serath's dive and GRIM.exe behind them. It would not guarantee the win, but it makes them beat our full team on our terms instead of a coin flip.

focus.title: Find Serath before the fight
focus.evidence: Serath finished without a death and took six of our ten deaths across the two late fights we lost.
focus.action: Before any late fight, one player names where Serath is, and the team commits only after that call. Check whether every fight after the last Fangtooth starts with it.

perPlayer.16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3: Goldilocks324's GRIM.exe ran over the enemy duo: Valmont died to GRIM.exe five times and Belica four, with farm above the usual pace and only three deaths. That is the carry job done. The ugly part is the order: GRIM.exe was our first death in both late fights we lost. Next game, when Serath goes airborne with Ascend, GRIM.exe holds Energy Shield for the landing and lets System Restore's health and speed carry the walk out.
perPlayer.7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b: Most healing in the lobby, thirteen wards against a usual of about ten, a hand in roughly two in five kills: Mr_Meat31 covered the support basics. The deaths are the leak. Four against a usual under three, and Serath took three, one in each late fight we lost. Every takedown hands Serath a cooldown-cutting visage, so a reachable healer is a gift. In late fights, Phase stays behind the frontline until Serath dives, and saves Blink for that landing.
perPlayer.a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c: Cuban Noobster's Aurora was the strongest game on our side. All three Fangtooths came our way, Aurora led the lobby in objective damage, farm and damage ran well over the usual Aurora pace, and Belica died to Aurora five times. Serath was the exception: never killed, and Aurora died to Serath twice. Next game, against a snowballing jungler, Aurora holds Cryoseism for that jungler's dive and freezes Serath on the landing, giving Hoarfrost a target that cannot walk away.
perPlayer.b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620: Kwang hit like a truck and folded like a lawn chair. Kumonguos put out the most hero damage on our side, well above that player's usual Kwang rate. The cost was eight deaths against a usual under six, and two came between fights shortly before each late fight we lost. Sequence, not proof. Late game, when Serath or Belica has not shown, Kwang saves Surge of the Heavens for the exit; the unselectable dash is the safest way out.
perPlayer.6ea14df4-52f3-463b-9d1f-2e42d2fff0ac: Near first-time on Wraith, Marlexa turned Renna into a spectator: three of Renna's four deaths came to Wraith, and Renna finished with a single item. Add twenty wards, the most in the lobby, and the second-most objective damage on our side. Strong shit. The late fights went the other way, with Serath killing Wraith in both. When Serath dives our backline next game, Wraith answers with Back It Up! on Serath, pulling Serath back to the dive's starting spot.

14.3.call: GRIM.exe killed Valmont, then Belica, won 2-0, and our first Fangtooth fell in the same window. Kill credits do not show who was at the pit.

16.6.call: Aurora killed Belica and GRIM.exe killed Valmont, won 2-0, and two of their outer towers fell in the same window. The timing does not show who hit the towers.

24.4.call: Aurora opened with a kill on Belica, then Serath took four of ours and we lost 1-5. Kwang had died shortly before; the record does not show why the fight was taken.

28.9.call: Belica killed GRIM.exe first, Serath took Wraith and Phase, and we lost 0-5 as our inner tower fell. Kill credits do not show positions or who started it.

16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.matchup: Duo lane was GRIM.exe with Phase into Lt. Belica with Valmont. Belica took first blood on GRIM.exe and Phase traded back on Valmont; early duo deaths ended even. After that the kill feed went our way. Belica built a physical basic-attack set and Valmont was their healer. The bigger threat sat in the jungle: Serath combined Sky Splitter lifesteal, Draconum's takedown healing and Salvation's low-health shield. GRIM.exe's passive turns basic attacks into magical damage, so Serath's Draconum armor does nothing against them; Terra's Vainglory was the only enemy magical armor.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.build: On the common winning core. Lightning Hawk builds Momentum while moving or attacking for an empowered, slowing hit; Plasma Blade stacks critical chance and Dust Devil stacks attack speed while hitting heroes, with movement speed at full stacks. Tainted Rounds cuts healing on basic attacks and adds on-hit damage that grows as the target's health falls, a real fit against Serath and Valmont's healing. Nuclear Rounds raises ability damage with critical chance, which feeds Displacement Blast and GTFO. Final inventory does not show purchase timing.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.eternal: Weald fires true-damage projectiles when GRIM.exe damages a hero below a health threshold, with more projectiles from bonus attack speed and a per-hero cooldown. Forage adds gold and experience per minion or monster kill, consistent with farm above the usual pace. Wind-Rider needs a dash, leap, teleport or stealth exit, and Pacifier's dash is GRIM.exe's only trigger. If late dives keep killing GRIM.exe first, Natural Resistance in place of Forage trades the farm bonus for a crowd control cleanse at low health; nothing here shows crowd control caused either death.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.augment: System Restore heals GRIM.exe and grants decaying movement speed whenever Energy Shield blocks an ability. That is the right tool against Serath's Ascend and Heaven's Fury, which are abilities, and against Belica's ability burst. The record does not show any blocks. Reboot.exe, cooldown reduction from Pulsefire, is the damage-side alternative; nothing in this match shows it would have done better.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.crest: Pacifier gives a dash and empowers the next physical damage instance, with extra damage against low-health targets and a recast after a quick kill. GRIM.exe's basic attacks deal magical damage, so the dash is the dependable half: it is GRIM.exe's only dash and the only Wind-Rider trigger. Spending it to chase leaves Energy Shield as the only defense when Serath arrives.
16f28434-561f-4f23-9454-40321f4a1ef3.improvement: Keep the core and Tainted Rounds. If Serath and Belica keep reaching GRIM.exe first in late fights, an armor item in place of Nuclear Rounds trades ability damage for survival against two physical attackers. This match does not prove which death that item would have prevented.

7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.matchup: Duo lane was Phase with GRIM.exe into Lt. Belica with Valmont. Valmont was the enemy healer and finished Tainted Scepter, which cuts healing on whoever Valmont hits with magical damage, including anyone Phase is healing. Belica killed Phase in the first-blood exchange; after that, Serath killed Phase three times. Serath, Belica and Terra all finished physical damage items.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.build: Marshal is on the support core and buffs Phase and nearby heroes with attack speed and on-hit damage, a direct fit for GRIM.exe. Tainted Totem cuts healing on anything Phase damages and passes that effect to allies Phase heals or shields, which matters against Serath's sustain. Prophecy and Spectra push Phase toward basic attacks: on-hit damage, attack speed and a missing-health true-damage burst. The core's Enra's Blessing and Galaxy Greaves were skipped, and no item adds armor.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.eternal: Exarch gives attack speed and on-hit magical damage to anyone Phase heals or shields, which suits a healer whose passive also heals the linked ally. Preservation raises healing and shielding Phase receives; Fervour heals Phase and nearby allies on basic attacks against heroes. With Serath ending three of Phase's lives, Delayed Fate is the slot-two alternative: part of incoming ability damage arrives as a damage over time, at the cost of Fervour's healing.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.augment: Psychic Support makes Essence Catalyst restore the linked ally's mana based on missing mana. GRIM.exe spends mana on Assault Mode basic attacks, so the fit is real when GRIM.exe is the link. The record does not show who Phase linked or how much mana it returned.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.crest: Tranquility heals Phase and nearby heroes with brief damage mitigation, raises the ward cap and pays gold over time while reducing minion gold. Thirteen wards and the lobby's top healing fit what the crest is for. Valmont ran the same crest.
7c8ab99c-31c5-4ea5-a6fa-e0d6417c3f1b.improvement: Supported conditional swap: if Serath keeps reaching Phase, Galaxy Greaves in place of Spectra gives physical and magical armor plus mana regeneration, giving up attack speed and the true-damage burst. Enra's Blessing, a shield on an immobilized ally nearby, is the other core comparison. Neither swap is proven to save a specific death.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.matchup: Jungle against Serath, a melee diver. Heaven's Fury marks a target and teleports Serath to it, Ascend dives from long range, and every takedown leaves a visage that cuts Serath's cooldowns, so kills snowball inside a fight. Serath finished without a death. Aurora's kill feed points at the gank targets that paid: Belica five times, Terra three, Renna once.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.build: On the common winning core. Spirit of Amir adds magical lifesteal in the jungle and magical power outside it, plus damage to monsters; Magnify shreds magical armor on ability hits; Spectral Schematics adds current-health damage whenever Aurora immobilizes a target. Dynamo and Elafrost add armor and health: Dynamo makes immobilized enemies take more damage, and Elafrost empowers a slowing basic attack after each ability. Two armor items against a physical Serath, Belica and Terra is a sound read.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.eternal: Lotus grants a random small bonus on a timer and on takedowns. Flawless heals Aurora and nearby allies once per ability cast that hits a hero, and Fragrance adds magical and true damage against heroes close by, which suits a melee jungler with a close-range Frost Storm. Immaculate, damage reduction while health is high, is the slot-two alternative against Serath's burst, giving up Fragrance's damage.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.augment: Glacial Thorns makes Glacial Charge leave crystals that damage and briefly root. Every root is another immobilize, which triggers Spectral Schematics and Dynamo and cuts the Frozen Simulacrum jump cooldown. The augment ties the whole build together; the record does not show how many crystals landed.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.crest: Tempest damages up to three nearby heroes every second for a few seconds and heals Aurora for part of it. It rewards staying inside a fight, which Aurora's armor supports. The record does not show when it was used.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.improvement: Keep it. The build fits the kit, the armor fits the enemy, and the lobby-leading objective damage gives no reason to change it. Our team already carried four anti-heal items, so Aurora does not need one for Serath. The open problem is Serath's dive, which is a crowd control timing call, not an item slot.

b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.matchup: Offlane against Terra, who built Mutilator, Fist of Razuul, Vainglory and Earthshaker: maximum-health damage, a healing empowered attack, and armors that grow while trading. Vainglory was the only magical armor on the enemy team. Terra killed Kwang three times and Kwang killed Terra twice; Belica and Serath added five more Kwang deaths. All three finished physical damage items.
b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.build: Magnify shreds magical armor on ability hits, which answers Vainglory directly, and adds health and omnivamp. Megacosm burns a share of maximum and bonus health over time on ability damage, a fit against Terra's health. Tainted Scepter cuts healing on magical damage. Orion converts item ability haste into attack speed and ramps on-hit damage on one target. The winning core's Oathkeeper was skipped, and no item adds armor while three enemies dealt physical damage.
b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.eternal: Knell's Rust stacks shred both armors on enemy heroes and hand Kwang part of what was shredded. Frequency adds attack speed and ability haste per Rust stack applied; Fracture adds damage against targets at maximum Rust. That is an all-in damage setup. Resonant Repair is the slot-two alternative, healing and tenacity whenever Kwang is immobilized, at the cost of Fracture's damage.
b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.augment: Aura of the Heavens grants Kwang omnivamp and nearby allies a smaller share. It stacks with Magnify's omnivamp and rewards fighting beside the team. The record does not show how much it healed.
b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.crest: Tempest pulses damage onto up to three nearby heroes for several seconds and returns part of it as healing. It suits a brawler who fights beside the team, and it stacks with the omnivamp from Magnify and Aura of the Heavens.
b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.improvement: Supported conditional swap: an armor item in place of Orion once the damage core is up. Terra, Serath and Belica all built physical damage, and eight deaths were the highest on our side. It gives up attack speed and on-hit ramp; this match does not prove which death it would have prevented.

6ea14df4-52f3-463b-9d1f-2e42d2fff0ac.matchup: Mid against Renna, who finished with one item, three deaths to Wraith and almost no hero damage. The lane threat disappeared early. The real threats came later: Serath killed Wraith twice, and Belica and Terra once each, all physical damage dealers.
6ea14df4-52f3-463b-9d1f-2e42d2fff0ac.build: On the common winning core plus Tainted Scepter. Soulbinder adds ability damage against heroes hit from long range and grows magical power each time it triggers, a natural fit for Knock, Knock! sniping. Noxia marks a hero on ability damage and bursts a share of maximum health when a second ability hits. Wraith Leggings adds magical penetration and extra ability damage against low-health heroes. Tainted Scepter cuts healing on magical damage, useful against Serath.
6ea14df4-52f3-463b-9d1f-2e42d2fff0ac.eternal: Lotus grants a random small bonus on a timer and on takedowns. Early Bloom adds an extra level at a level breakpoint, and Immaculate reduces damage while health is high, which suits a sniper who should be shooting from full health. It is gone after the first hit of a dive. Keep it; nothing here shows a better slot.
6ea14df4-52f3-463b-9d1f-2e42d2fff0ac.augment: Mystic Marksman turns Knock, Knock! into magical damage, so every magical item in the build applies to the sniper shot. Sniper's Bounty, extra gold on Knock, Knock! killing blows, is the alternative for a greedier game; the record cannot say which would have mattered more.
6ea14df4-52f3-463b-9d1f-2e42d2fff0ac.crest: Epoch puts Wraith into stasis briefly. Against Serath, whose Heaven's Fury strikes repeatedly before teleporting in, stasis is the tool that buys time for help. The record does not show whether it was available in either late fight.
6ea14df4-52f3-463b-9d1f-2e42d2fff0ac.improvement: Keep the build. All four Wraith deaths came to physical attackers, and two came inside lost late fights, so a defensive comparison is the only one worth making: an armor item in place of Wraith Leggings gives up low-health finishing damage for survival. Nothing in this match proves that trade.

a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.crest: Tempest damages up to three nearby heroes every second for a few seconds and heals Aurora for part of it. It rewards staying inside a fight, which Aurora's armor supports. The record does not show when it was used.
a0c393cc-1437-4bdc-8168-64676ce2166c.improvement: Keep it. The build fits the kit, the armor fits the enemy, and the lobby-leading objective damage gives no reason to change it. Our team already carried four anti-heal items, so Aurora does not need one for Serath. The open problem is Serath's dive, which is a crowd control timing call, not an item slot.

b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.matchup: Offlane against Terra, who built Mutilator, Fist of Razuul, Vainglory and Earthshaker: maximum-health damage, a healing empowered attack, and armors that grow while trading. Vainglory was the only magical armor on the enemy team. Terra killed Kwang three times and Kwang killed Terra twice; Belica and Serath added five more Kwang deaths. All three finished physical damage items.
b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.build: Magnify shreds magical armor on ability hits, which answers Vainglory directly, and adds health and omnivamp. Megacosm burns a share of maximum and bonus health over time on ability damage, a fit against Terra's health. Tainted Scepter cuts healing on magical damage. Orion converts item ability haste into attack speed and ramps on-hit damage on one target. The winning core's Oathkeeper was skipped, and no item adds armor while three enemies dealt physical damage.
b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.eternal: Knell's Rust stacks shred both armors on enemy heroes and hand Kwang part of what was shredded. Frequency adds attack speed and ability haste per Rust stack applied; Fracture adds damage against targets at maximum Rust. That is an all-in damage setup. Resonant Repair is the slot-two alternative, healing and tenacity whenever Kwang is immobilized, at the cost of Fracture's damage.
b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.augment: Aura of the Heavens grants Kwang omnivamp and nearby allies a smaller share. It stacks with Magnify's omnivamp and rewards fighting beside the team. The record does not show how much it healed.
b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.crest: Tempest pulses damage onto up to three nearby heroes for several seconds and returns part of it as healing. It suits a brawler who fights beside the team, and it stacks with the omnivamp from Magnify and Aura of the Heavens.
b449674d-1061-4984-b85e-5acf60f0d620.improvement: Supported conditional swap: an armor item in place of Orion once the damage core is up. Terra, Serath and Belica all built physical damage, and eight deaths were the highest on our side. It gives up attack speed and on-hit ramp; this match does not prove which death it would have prevented.

6ea14df4-52f3-463b-9d1f-2e42d2fff0ac.matchup: Mid against Renna, who finished with one item, three deaths to Wraith and almost no hero damage. The lane threat disappeared early. The real threats came later: Serath killed Wraith twice, and Belica and Terra once each, all physical damage dealers.
6ea14df4-52f3-463b-9d1f-2e42d2fff0ac.build: On the common winning core plus Tainted Scepter. Soulbinder adds ability damage against heroes hit from long range and grows magical power each time it triggers, a natural fit for Knock, Knock! sniping. Noxia marks a hero on ability damage and bursts a share of maximum health when a second ability hits. Wraith Leggings adds magical penetration and extra ability damage against low-health heroes. Tainted Scepter cuts healing on magical damage, useful against Serath.
6ea14df4-52f3-463b-9d1f-2e42d2fff0ac.eternal: Lotus grants a random small bonus on a timer and on takedowns. Early Bloom adds an extra level at a level breakpoint, and Immaculate reduces damage while health is high, which suits a sniper who should be shooting from full health. It is gone after the first hit of a dive. Keep it; nothing here shows a better slot.
6ea14df4-52f3-463b-9d1f-2e42d2fff0ac.augment: Mystic Marksman turns Knock, Knock! into magical damage, so every magical item in the build applies to the sniper shot. Sniper's Bounty, extra gold on Knock, Knock! killing blows, is the alternative for a greedier game; the record cannot say which would have mattered more.
6ea14df4-52f3-463b-9d1f-2e42d2fff0ac.crest: Epoch puts Wraith into stasis briefly. Against Serath, whose Heaven's Fury strikes repeatedly before teleporting in, stasis is the tool that buys time for help. The record does not show whether it was available in either late fight.
6ea14df4-52f3-463b-9d1f-2e42d2fff0ac.improvement: Keep the build. All four Wraith deaths came to physical attackers, and two came inside lost late fights, so a defensive comparison is the only one worth making: an armor item in place of Wraith Leggings gives up low-health finishing damage for survival. Nothing in this match proves that trade.
